title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-1 Art & Culture PART-1

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is associated with the term ‘ties of protection’?
questions.solution:
Raksha Bandhan is a Hindu festival that literally translates to the 'bond of protection' or 'ties of protection'. It celebrates the relationship between brothers and sisters, where the sister ties a sacred thread called a Rakhi on the brother's wrist.

Note: In return, the brother pledges to protect her and offers gifts as a token of love.

questions.question: Banganga festival takes place annually at which of the following places in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The Banganga Festival is an annual music and cultural festival organized by the Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (MTDC) at Malabar Hill, Mumbai. It takes place at the historic Banganga Tank, which is believed to have been created by a bow-shot from Lord Rama.

Additional Info: The festival showcases classical music performances by renowned artists in a serene, heritage environment.

questions.question: The Hemis Festival is widely celebrated in which state of India?
questions.solution:
The Hemis Festival is one of the most famous cultural events in Ladakh, celebrated at the Hemis Gompa (monastery). It commemorates the birth anniversary of Lord Padmasambhava, the founder of Tibetan Buddhism.

Key Feature: The festival is known for its vibrant Cham Dance (masked dance) performed by monks to the sound of traditional drums and horns.

questions.question:
This festival was started by the Government of Nagaland in 2000 to encourage interaction among tribes
and to promote the cultural heritage of the State. Identify the festival.
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival is often called the 'Festival of Festivals'. It was launched by the Government of Nagaland in 2000 to promote inter-tribal interaction and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the Naga tribes.

Context: It is held annually from December 1 to 10 at the Kisama Heritage Village, coinciding with Nagaland Statehood Day.

questions.question: During which festival is Garba performed?
questions.solution:
Garba is a high-energy folk dance originating from Gujarat, traditionally performed during the nine-day Navratri festival. Dancers move in circles around a lit lamp or an image of Goddess Durga to symbolize the cycle of life.

Note: In 2023, UNESCO inscribed Garba of Gujarat on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

questions.question: The Hemis Festival has an influence of which religion?
questions.solution:
The Hemis Festival is deeply rooted in Buddhism, specifically the Tibetan Buddhist tradition. It celebrates the victory of good over evil through spiritual rituals and performances by the Lamas.

Cultural Fact: Every 12 years, the festival features the public display of a giant Thangka (religious painting) of Guru Padmasambhava.

questions.question: In which state is the Chithirai festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Chithirai Festival is a grand month-long celebration held in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. It re-enacts the wedding of Goddess Meenakshi (a form of Parvati) and Lord Sundareswarar (a form of Shiva).

Visual Note: The festival involves a massive procession of the deity Lord Alagar entering the Vaigai River.

questions.question: The activity of making a human pyramid and putting efforts to break an earthen pot filled with buttermilk is associated with which festival?
questions.solution:
The Dahi Handi ritual, where human pyramids are formed to break a pot of buttermilk, is a core part of Janmashtami (the birth of Lord Krishna). This tradition mimics Krishna's childhood antics of stealing butter with his friends.

Note: It is most enthusiastically celebrated in states like Maharashtra and Gujarat.

questions.question: In which city of Assam is the Tea Festival celebrated every year?
questions.solution:
The Tea Festival is organized annually in Jorhat, which is known as the 'Tea Capital of the World'. This festival highlights the tea industry of Assam, featuring tea tasting sessions, ethnic food, and traditional sports.

Fact: Jorhat is home to the Tocklai Tea Research Institute, one of the oldest tea research centers globally.

questions.question: Which of the following states organises ‘Lokrang’, a five-day festival, beginning every year on 26 January?
questions.solution:
Lokrang is a major folk festival organized by the Madhya Pradesh Tribal Museum in Bhopal. Starting on Republic Day (January 26), it lasts for five days and showcases the folk and tribal arts, dances, and crafts of Madhya Pradesh and other states.

Objective: The festival aims to bridge the gap between urban life and rural tribal traditions.

questions.question: Which festival traces its origin to the Tibetan New Year and in Ladakh, it is celebrated every year at the end of the harvesting season?
questions.solution:
Losar is the Tibetan New Year festival, celebrated with great fervor in Ladakh. It marks the end of the harvest season and the beginning of the new year according to the lunisolar calendar.

Ritual: Families clean their homes, prepare special dishes like Guthuk, and perform traditional dances to drive away evil spirits.

questions.question: The ‘Kambala’ festival is organised by farming communities in the state of _________.
questions.solution:
Kambala is a traditional buffalo race held in the coastal districts of Karnataka. It is a sport practiced by the farming communities as a tribute to the gods for a good harvest.

Note: The race takes place in slushy paddy fields, and it is a significant display of rural strength and coordination.

questions.question: In which district of Gujarat is the Modhera dance festival organised by the Government of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The Modhera Dance Festival (also known as Uttarardh Mahotsav) is held at the historic Sun Temple in Mehsana district, Gujarat. It is organized during the third week of January, following the Uttarayan festival.

Context: The temple, built during the Chaulukya dynasty, serves as a stunning backdrop for classical dance performances from across India.

questions.question: The Sirpur National Dance and Music Festival is organised every year in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The Sirpur National Dance and Music Festival is held in Chhattisgarh. It takes place at the archaeological site of Sirpur, known for its 7th-century Laxman Temple.

Goal: The festival promotes the historical and cultural significance of Sirpur as a major center for Buddhism and Hinduism in ancient times.

questions.question: Celebrated every year, the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award festival is named after the famous classical dancer of which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was the legendary doyen of Odissi dance. The award festival is held annually in Bhubaneswar to honor his legacy and contributions to the revival of this classical dance form.

Note: He was instrumental in codifying the Odissi style and was the first person from Odisha to receive the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: Which country celebrates one of the famous festivals known as Paro Tschechu?
questions.solution:
Paro Tschechu is one of the biggest and most popular religious festivals in Bhutan. It is held in the Paro valley and features spectacular mask dances performed by monks and laymen.

Key Event: The festival concludes with the unfurling of a giant silk Thangka called a Thongdrel, which is said to wash away sins.

questions.question: The Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhorh Divas which coincides with which Hindu festival?
questions.solution:
Bandi Chhorh Divas (Day of Liberation) is a Sikh festival that celebrates the release of Guru Hargobind Ji from Gwalior Fort in 1619. It coincides with the Hindu festival of Diwali.

Tradition: Both festivals involve the lighting of lamps (Deepmala) and fireworks, symbolizing the victory of freedom and light over darkness.

questions.question: Which state is famous for celebrating the Majuli festival?
questions.solution:
The Majuli Festival is celebrated on Majuli Island in Assam, which is the world's largest river island. The festival showcases the unique Neo-Vaishnavite culture of the island, including Sattriya dances and tribal crafts.

Note: It provides a platform for the various ethnic groups of Majuli to display their heritage.

questions.question: The ten-day festival of Bastar Dussehra is associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Bastar Dussehra is a unique 75-day long festival celebrated in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Unlike the standard Dussehra, it is not about the victory of Rama over Ravana but is dedicated to the local deity, Danteshwari Devi.

Fact: It is considered one of the longest festivals in the world.

questions.question: Doongri festival of Himachal Pradesh is primarily celebrated by which religious community?
questions.solution:
The Doongri Festival (also known as the Hadimba Devi Mela) is a major Hindu festival celebrated in Manali, Himachal Pradesh. It celebrates the birthday of Goddess Hadimba, the patron deity of the region and the wife of Bhima from the Mahabharata.

Celebration: It involves colorful processions and folk dances during the spring season.

questions.question: Tamladu is a festival celebrated by the Buddhist community of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Tamladu is a significant festival celebrated by the Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It is an ancient festival where people pray to nature gods and ancestors for the protection of crops and the well-being of the community.

Note: While the question mentions the 'Buddhist community', it is primarily an indigenous tribal festival of the Digaru Mishmis.

questions.question: How many times in a year is the Bihu festival celebrated in Assam?
questions.solution:
The Bihu festival is celebrated three times in a year in Assam to mark different stages of the agricultural cycle:
1. Rongali (Bohag) Bihu: Celebrates the New Year and spring (April).
2. Kongali (Kati) Bihu: A solemn festival involving lamps to protect crops (October).
3. Bhogali (Magh) Bihu: A harvest festival with community feasts (January).

questions.question: Guruvayur Ekadashi is the cultural festival of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Guruvayur Ekadashi is a prestigious cultural and religious festival celebrated at the Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple in Kerala. It occurs during the month of Vrischikam (Nov-Dec).

Highlight: A grand elephant procession (Gajapooja) is held to honor the temple's famous elephant, Guruvayur Keshavan.

questions.question: Which festival has the meaning ‘to boil’ or ‘boiling’ in its name?
questions.solution:
The name Pongal is derived from the Tamil word 'Pongu', which means 'to boil' or 'spilling over'. This refers to the traditional ritual of boiling fresh rice in milk and jaggery until it overflows the pot, signifying prosperity and abundance.

Context: It is a harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states, is Makar Sankranti celebrated by the name of ‘Magha Saaji’?
questions.solution:
In Himachal Pradesh, the festival of Makar Sankranti is locally known as Magha Saaji. 'Magha' refers to the Hindu month, and 'Saaji' is the local word for Sankranti (the start of the month).

Traditions: People take holy dips in rivers like the Satluj and Beas and enjoy special meals including Khichdi and Ghee.
